title: wg: propose the IRCv3 METADATA 'identity' key, with meshIRCd and mimid as the two implementations
notes:
Verified against ircv3.net and the specifications repo's CONTRIBUTING, 2026-11-22.

HOW IRCV3 WORKS. An open working group, not a membership body: 'Contributions are welcome from anyone in the IRC community; including users, developers, operators, administrators.' Decisions by consensus, a WG Chair facilitating when consensus fails. Two places to participate: the ircv3/ircv3-specifications GitHub repo, and #ircv3 on irc.libera.chat. To be a LISTED contributor a project must demonstrate support of the IRCv3 specifications, have the approval of the current contributors, and follow the code of conduct.

THE PROCESS HAS THREE STAGES.
1. ircv3-ideas: for a concept without a concrete spec or reference implementation. No stakeholder requirements.
2. ircv3-specifications: needs a stakeholder of the WG to propose or sponsor it, a specification describing all intended behaviour, and at least one implementation that is downloadable or accessible online, backwards compatible.
3. Ratification: at least TWO server implementations (or one bouncer for a bouncer-specific spec), at least ONE client implementation, and WG stakeholder approval.

TWO THINGS THIS CHANGES.

First, the identity key starts in ircv3-ideas, not specifications: mimid is not yet a listed contributor and so cannot sponsor its own proposal at stage 2. mimid already implements message-tags, server-time, echo-message, chathistory, SASL, CAP and soju.im/webpush, which is the evidence for 'demonstrates support of the IRCv3 specifications' when asking to be listed.

Second, ratification needs a CLIENT implementation, and there is none: meshIRCd and mimid are the two servers, but nothing on the client side shows a DID. That gap has to be filled or the proposal cannot ratify however good it is.

AND A WARNING ABOUT THE FOUNDATION. metadata-2 is work-in-progress, and it succeeds an abandoned one: ircv3.net says the v3.2 METADATA command 'was found to have issues related to rate-limiting and excessive notifications, which made it impossible for servers in widespread use to implement.' So an identity key built on METADATA inherits a mechanism that already failed once in widespread servers.

THE CHEAPER FIRST STEP, worth considering before any spec work: WHOIS numeric 320 carries free-form text and needs no specification at all. meshIRCd and mimid already agree on 'DID <uri>' and 'Verified true/false' there (bead mimid-i0id.11). Two servers can share that convention today, and a client can read it today, with no process. The spec work is only needed for METADATA, which is the part at risk.
